title: The Signature Interview Protocol
body:
The Signature Interview Protocol is a seven-gate preparation system: research the company, bank twelve stories, run mock rounds, assemble an evidence file, prepare questions for them, lock logistics, and write a recovery plan for tough moments. Each gate has a done-criterion, so preparation is checkable instead of vibes.

The protocol treats interviewing as a project with a definition of done. Gate three, mock rounds, uses the Assistant-Maker Mock Interviewer to simulate pressure. Gate seven, the recovery plan, scripts exactly what you say when a question blanks you, because blanking is predictable and therefore preparable.

It is labeled Signature because the gate structure and done-criteria are Signature-original, built for Manon's standard that preparation is measurable.

Key facts: Seven gates, each with a done-criterion; Mock rounds under simulated pressure; Scripted recovery for blank moments; Signature-original preparation system.

Real-world examples: Interview preparation, Signature systems.

title: JAH Answer Forge
body:
The JAH Answer Forge turns raw experience into STAR+ answers: situation, task, action, result, plus the extra beat of what you would do differently now. That final beat is what separates a story from a lesson.

Forging is mechanical: feed in the messy memory, and the forge extracts the decision you made, the numbers that prove it, and the principle it taught you. Weak stories fail at the forge for identifiable reasons, usually a missing decision or a missing number, and get rebuilt.

Every story in the bank passes through the forge before it is allowed near an interview.

Key facts: STAR plus the what-I-would-change beat; Extracts decision, numbers, principle; Diagnoses weak stories mechanically; Every banked story is forged.

Real-world examples: STAR method, Story banking.

demo.code:
function forge(s,t,a,r){return {S:'Situation: '+s,T:'Task: '+t,A:'Action: '+a,R:'Result: '+r,plus:'what I would do differently now'}};
console.log(JSON.stringify({system:'JAH Answer Forge',answer:forge('deadline slipped','I owned the timeline','re-scoped with the client daily','shipped on the revised date')}));
demo.verified_output: {"system":"JAH Answer Forge","answer":{"S":"Situation: deadline slipped","T":"Task: I owned the timeline","A":"Action: re-scoped with the client daily","R":"Result: shipped on the revised date","plus":"what I would do differently now"}}

title: Hither-Thither Answer Weave
body:
The Hither-Thither Answer Weave braids three threads into one answer: a metric that proves, a story that humanizes, and a lesson that generalizes. One thread alone is thin; woven together they are hard to forget.

In practice you open with the metric, land the story, and close with the lesson, all inside ninety seconds. The weave keeps answers from drifting into pure anecdote or pure numbers.

It is the Signature answer shape: proof, humanity, and principle in one pass.

Key facts: Metric, story, lesson in one answer; Ninety-second weave; Proof plus humanity plus principle; Signature-original answer shape.

Real-world examples: Answer structure, Storytelling.

demo.code:
function weave(threads){return threads.join(' | ');}
console.log(JSON.stringify({system:'Hither-Thither Answer Weave',woven:weave(['metric: cut load time 40%','story: the outage night','lesson: monitor the deploy'])}));
demo.verified_output: {"system":"Hither-Thither Answer Weave","woven":"metric: cut load time 40% | story: the outage night | lesson: monitor the deploy"}

title: The Mirror Answer
body:
The Mirror Answer starts from the employer's side of the table: every question is really can this person do the job, and will they stay and thrive here. Answer the asked question, but aim every story at those two hidden ones.

For why should we hire you, the mirror shows the hiring manager's risk: a wrong hire costs months. Your answer should retire that risk with evidence of the exact work and the exact environment fit.

Candidates who answer the mirror get hired; candidates who answer only the surface get liked.

Key facts: Every question hides: can they do it, will they stay; Retire the hiring risk with evidence; Answer surface, aim at the mirror; Employer-side framing.

Real-world examples: Interview strategy, Persuasion.

demo.code:
function mirror(q){return {their_question:q,employer_thinks:'can this person do the job and stay?',your_angle:'prove both in one story'};}
console.log(JSON.stringify({system:'Mirror Answer',...mirror('why should we hire you?')}));

title: God-Mode Interview Ladder
body:
The God-Mode Interview Ladder climbs preparation through seven rungs: simple answers first, then competitive polish, then mix-and-match story combinations, then unmade answers to questions you invent, then top-notch delivery, future-grade presence, and finally god-mode calm.

Each rung has drills: week one is story banking, week two is timed mocks, week three is hostile questions. You do not attempt god-mode calm before the stories exist; the ladder enforces the order.

It applies the generator ladder to the candidate: progression, not cramming.

Key facts: Seven rungs from simple to god-mode; Drills per rung, order enforced; Timed mocks before hostile questions; Progression, not cramming.

Real-world examples: Preparation plans, Generator ladder.
facts: Seven rungs from simple to god-mode

title: Archive-Aware Candidate Dossier
body:
The Archive-Aware Candidate Dossier is your evidence file: every claim on the resume paired with its proof, performance reviews, shipped links, numbers with sources. If you cannot produce the evidence, the claim leaves the resume.

Interviewers probe exactly where evidence is thinnest, so the dossier tells you where you are strong before they do. The drift-checker flags claims that outgrew their proof.

It turns the resume from assertions into an archive.

Key facts: Every claim paired with evidence; Unprovable claims removed; Shows your strong ground before they probe; Resume as archive.

Real-world examples: Resumes, Evidence.

title: Fresh-Session First Impression
body:
The Fresh-Session First Impression treats the interview's first five minutes as a clean session: no stale assumptions from the commute, the last interview, or the news. You arrive early, put the phone away, and load exactly one thing, your ninety-second story.

Presence is a feature you can rehearse: warm alert energy, the prepared opener, and genuine curiosity about the interviewer. First impressions form in seconds and anchor everything after.

It is the human version of the fresh-session screen: nothing carries over except what you choose.

Key facts: First five minutes as a clean session; One loaded thing: the ninety-second story; Warm, alert, curious energy; Anchors everything that follows.

Real-world examples: Presence, Interview openings.

console.log(JSON.stringify({system:'Fresh-Session First Impression',checklist:firstImpression()}));

title: Exhaustive Answer Pill
body:
The Exhaustive Answer Pill expands one banked story into four depths: the base version, the version with numbers, the version that includes a failure, and the thirty-second compressed version. Whatever the interviewer digs for, you have the depth.

Most candidates have one depth and stall when probed. The pill means follow-up questions meet prepared material instead of improvisation.

Depth beats breadth: four versions of twelve stories beats one version of fifty.

Key facts: Four depths per story; Base, numbers, failure, compressed; Follow-ups meet prepared material; Depth over breadth.

Real-world examples: Story banking, Follow-up questions.

demo.code:
function exhaustive(base){return [base,base+' — with numbers',base+' — with a failure in it',base+' — as a 30-second version'];}
console.log(JSON.stringify({system:'Exhaustive Answer Pill',versions:exhaustive('tell me about yourself')}));

title: Million-March Preparation Counter
body:
The Million-March Preparation Counter tracks story banking like a march: twelve stories is the target, and the counter shows percent complete, derived from the bank itself. Preparation you can see is preparation you finish.

Each story counts only when forged, timed, and mock-tested. The counter refuses partial credit, which is why the bank is actually ready instead of theoretically ready.

It applies the march discipline to the candidate: derived counts, honest progress.

Key facts: Twelve forged stories as the target; Counts only forged, timed, tested stories; Derived from the bank, never estimated; Honest progress over vibes.

Real-world examples: Preparation tracking, Story banking.

title: Drift-Check Your Resume
body:
Drift-Check Your Resume scans every resume claim against reality: inflated titles, skills you touched once, numbers you cannot source. Flagged claims get removed or reworded before an interviewer finds them.

Resumes drift because each edit adds a little polish and nobody audits. The checker is the audit: exact-duplicate responsibilities merged, superlatives challenged, dates verified.

An interview is a verification process; the checker runs it first.

Key facts: Flags inflated titles and unsourced numbers; Merges duplicated responsibilities; Challenges superlatives; Audit before they audit you.

Real-world examples: Resumes, Verification.

title: Full-File Portfolio Rule
body:
The Full-File Portfolio Rule says every portfolio piece is the complete work with context, not a screenshot and a caption. Case studies carry the problem, the constraints, the decisions, and the outcome.

Interviewers skim portfolios in minutes; complete files let them go deep on exactly one piece, which is where hiring decisions happen. A portfolio of teasers invites no second look.

It is the full-file promise applied to the candidate.

Key facts: Complete work with full context; Problem, constraints, decisions, outcome; Built for the deep dive on one piece; No teasers.

Real-world examples: Portfolios, Case studies.

title: Provenance of Claims
body:
Provenance of Claims seals every number you will say out loud: cut load time forty percent seals to the deploy log, led four engineers seals to the org chart. If challenged, you produce the source, not a memory.

Candidates lose credibility on exactly one exaggerated number. Sealing forces the discipline beforehand: every metric gets its origin recorded while the memory is fresh.

In the interview, calm citation beats confident vagueness.

Key facts: Every number sealed to its source; Produce the origin when challenged; Recorded while memory is fresh; Calm citation over vague confidence.

Real-world examples: Credibility, Metrics.

title: On-Device Calm
body:
On-Device Calm is the composure system: route the adrenaline like Standard 1.0 routes a question, to preparation instead of panic. Nerves are energy without a task; give them the task.

The mechanics are physical and boring: slow exhale before answering, pause instead of filler words, water on the table. Boring works because interviews are won on clarity, not charisma.

Calm is not the absence of nerves; it is nerves with a routing table.

Key facts: Route adrenaline to preparation; Slow exhale, pause over filler; Physical mechanics, boring and effective; Clarity over charisma.

Real-world examples: Composure, Interview nerves.

demo.code:
function route(q){const l=q.toLowerCase();if(l.includes('find'))return 'lookup';if(l.includes('make')||l.includes('generate'))return 'generate';return 'converse';}
console.log(JSON.stringify({system:'On-Device Calm',routes:['find my story bank','generate a mock round','I am nervous'].map(route),key:'none'}));

title: The Direct Question
body:
The Direct Question drill practices answering the bluntest version straight: what will you actually do here, why did you leave, what are you bad at. No deflection, one breath, plainly.

Deflection is detectable and it reads as hiding. The drill builds the muscle of the direct answer: acknowledge, answer, stop. Stopping is the hard part.

Manon's standard applied to candidates: plain speech, no theater.

Key facts: Practice the bluntest questions; Acknowledge, answer, stop; No deflection, no theater; Plain speech as discipline.

Real-world examples: Interview drills, Honesty.

title: Assistant-Maker Mock Interviewer
body:
The Assistant-Maker Mock Interviewer is a personal AI built for your prep: wired to your story bank, it runs mock rounds, scores answers against the forge criteria, and gets harsher each round like a real panel.

Because it is yours, it knows your weak stories and attacks them. Because it is tireless, round ten happens at midnight if you want it.

It is the assistant-maker feature aimed at the highest-stakes conversation of your career.

Key facts: Wired to your story bank; Scores against forge criteria; Escalating harshness per round; Tireless midnight mocks.

Real-world examples: Mock interviews, AI coaching.

title: Teach-Ladder Skill Proof
body:
Teach-Ladder Skill Proof demonstrates skill at the right rung: simple skills get simple demos, complex skills get architecture walkthroughs. Claiming senior skill with junior proof fails the ladder.

For system design that means whiteboarding tradeoffs, not reciting definitions. For debugging it means narrating a real incident. The rung must match the claim.

Show, at the right altitude, not tell.

Key facts: Proof matched to claimed rung; System design: tradeoffs, not definitions; Debugging: narrate a real incident; Show at the right altitude.

Real-world examples: Skill assessment, Technical interviews.
